svg.text: Dual-Hub ExpressRoute Segregation: Firewall Air-Gap (1.B) & Dual vHub (1.D)
ExpressRoute Circuit C1 (Prod VRF / Bandwidth SLA)
Isolates north-south Prod traffic from Non-Prod bursts
vWAN 1.D: Outbound Route Map tags 65001:100 or drops VNet 2
On-Premises Prod VRF / CE Router Pair 1
CRITICAL: Filter Azure 10.x so CE never re-advertises to C2!
VNet 1 <-> VNet 2 direct peering (no Gateway Transit).
Pros: Zero BGP policy; system route beats MSEE.
Cons: O(N^2) peering mesh; bypasses Hub Firewalls.
Pattern 1.D: Dual Secured Virtual WAN Hubs
1. Steady state: vHub 1 prefers local C1; vHub 2
prefers local C2; E-W rides Microsoft inter-hub.
2. Automatic failover: If C1 drops, vHub 1 routes
across inter-hub link to vHub 2 -> C2!
3. Set Hub Routing Preference = AS Path so Global
Reach prepends never beat inter-hub transit.
4. Compatible with Secured vHub Routing Intent
(Pattern 1.C achieves this in non-vWAN via ARS)
ExpressRoute Circuit C2 (Non-Prod VRF / Bulk Link)
Contains dev/test/backup transfers onto C2 bandwidth
vWAN 1.D: Outbound Route Map tags 65001:200 or drops VNet 1
On-Premises Non-Prod VRF / CE Router Pair 2
Shared On-Prem IPs (AD/DNS) safely reachable from both hubs!
Optional Direct Spoke Peering (1.A - Bypasses Hub Firewalls)
